bodies.name: Varuna
bodies.credit: Fernández-Valenzuela et al. (2019), ApJL; multi-epoch rotational photometry
bodies.shapeMeaning: Illustrative scale model of the published Jacobi fit: b/a=0.60, c/b=0.72, scaled to the paper’s adopted approximate 700 km volume-equivalent diameter. These smooth axes are inferred, not resolved terrain.
bodies.orientationMeaning: Uses one published pole interpretation, ecliptic longitude 53° ±10° and latitude −64° ±6°, converted with the J2000 mean obliquity for display. The antipodal pole is also allowed; equinox and meridian are display conventions, not a qualified absolute attitude.
bodies.periodText: About 6.34357 hours from photometry; display phase is illustrative
bodies.introduction: Varuna’s rapid rotation and changing brightness reveal an elongated world beyond Neptune. This smooth model follows a published light-curve fit; its absolute size remains approximate.

numericEvidence.scaleMeaning: The same paper adopts approximately 700 km volume-equivalent diameter for its satellite discussion; this is an approximate model scale, not an occultation-derived 3D diameter.

unresolved: Absolute dimensions remain uncertain: thermal scale and the reported 2010 occultation chord are in tension.
The shortest axis depends on hydrostatic equilibrium; the data also allow a nearby non-equilibrium fit.
The 2019 satellite signal is a candidate, not a qualified companion for this package.

bodies.name: Varda
bodies.credit: Proudfoot et al. (2026), occult3d reanalysis of Souami et al. (2020) occultation chords
bodies.shapeMeaning: One published allowable triaxial model, with semiaxes 389, 353 and 248 km. The line-of-sight depth is unconstrained; these best-fit values illustrate a solution rather than a uniquely measured body shape.
bodies.orientationMeaning: Assumes the spin pole aligns with Ilmarë’s orbit: J2000 RA 272.6° and declination −10.8°. This is a model prior; rotational phase and meridian are illustrative.
bodies.periodText: Unresolved; photometric aliases and synchronous rotation remain alternatives
bodies.introduction: Varda is a distant binary-system primary whose outline was measured as it eclipsed a star. Its companion’s orbit helps orient this model, but Varda’s depth remains uncertain.

numericEvidence.section: Proudfoot et al. (2026), Table 1, Table 3, Figure 4 and section 5.2
numericEvidence.axisUncertaintyMeaning: The paper intentionally reports only an example best fit for Varda: c/a is unconstrained. No axis confidence interval or precise physical volume is asserted.
numericEvidence.radiusFormula: cbrt(389 * 353 * 248); volume-equivalent radius of this displayed model only
numericEvidence.poleMeaning: J2000 equatorial orbit-pole prior, not an independently observed surface pole

unresolved: Depth and volume are not uniquely measured; many c/a values remain possible.
Spin-orbit alignment is assumed, and no absolute phase or sidereal period is installed.
Additional 2018 occultation chords mentioned in conference proceedings were not publicly released in the 2026 analysis.

bodies.name: Máni
bodies.credit: Rommel et al. (2023), A&A 678, A167; nine stellar-occultation campaigns
bodies.shapeMeaning: Silhouette-constrained oblate approximation: the observed 824 ×770 km projected ellipse is represented by full axes 824 ×824 ×770 km. The equal equatorial depth and equator-on interpretation are assumptions; true flattening may be larger.
bodies.orientationMeaning: Illustrative pole RA 0°, declination 90° and arbitrary meridian; the occultation position angle does not determine an inertial spin pole.
bodies.periodText: Unresolved; published alternatives include 7.33 and 10.44 hours
bodies.introduction: Formerly 2002 MS4, Máni has an outline measured through many stellar occultations. One event revealed a large depression along its edge, but its global terrain and three-dimensional shape remain unresolved.

numericEvidence.section: Rommel et al. (2023), 2020 August 8 ellipse fit and section 4
numericEvidence.axisOrdering: The two equal 824 km full axes are the assumed equator; the 770 km full axis is the minimum-flattening polar interpretation of the projected limb.
numericEvidence.radiusFormula: cbrt(412 * 412 * 385); model volume radius, distinct from the measured area-equivalent radius 398 km
numericEvidence.namingReference: WGSBN Bulletin 5(11), 2025 June 9, page 13: (307261) Máni = 2002 MS4

unresolved: The occultations measure projected limbs, not depth; true oblateness and spin pole remain unresolved.
Observed limb depressions are not a global elevation map and are not extruded around the model.
Rotational period alternatives and doubled aliases are unresolved.

bodies.name: Achlys
bodies.credit: Dias-Oliveira et al. (2017), AJ 154, 22; four stellar occultations
bodies.shapeMeaning: Published Jacobi-ellipsoid interpretation, with semiaxes 470 ±20, 383 ±10 and 245 ±8 km. It assumes hydrostatic equilibrium and a 6.75-hour rotation; the smooth shape is inferred from occultations, not imaged terrain.
bodies.orientationMeaning: Illustrative pole RA 0°, declination 90° and arbitrary meridian. The paper’s local projected-limb and opening angles do not provide a unique absolute surface attitude for this display.
bodies.periodText: About 6.75 hours in the adopted shape interpretation; display phase is illustrative
bodies.introduction: Formerly 2003 AZ84, Achlys is a plutino in Neptune’s 3:2 orbital resonance. Its changing occultation silhouette supports a flattened, elongated model, while a grazing event hints at a local depression.

numericEvidence.section: Dias-Oliveira et al. (2017), section IV.2 and conclusions
numericEvidence.radiusFormula: cbrt(470 * 383 * 245); volume-equivalent model radius, not the paper’s projected area-equivalent radius 386 ±6 km
modelAssumptions: Single-peaked 6.75-hour modulation attributed to albedo variation
Fixed pole between 2012 and 2014 within limited aspect changes
numericEvidence.namingReference: WGSBN Bulletin 5(15), 2025 June 30, page 16: (208996) Achlys = 2003 AZ84

unresolved: The hydrostatic-equilibrium interpretation is conditional; no precise absolute spin attitude is supplied.
A limb depression admits several profiles; it is not reproduced as fabricated global topography.
